as_told.title: Malmgren handles debris from Gise's desk

plain: In the early 1960s in New Mexico, Lawrence Preston Gise, head of the Albuquerque branch of the Atomic Energy Commission, told a young government economist named Harold Malmgren that the US had been recovering crashed UFOs and trying to reverse engineer them, meaning take them apart to learn how they were built. Then, Malmgren says, Gise "reached for some stuff sitting on his desk" and said, "These are things that have come down," including a "round rock", and Malmgren held the pieces in his hands. Malmgren, who later became a presidential adviser, tells it first-hand; the writer Matthew Pines and Michels both repeat it from him, with Michels citing Malmgren's posts and noting that Gise was Jeff Bezos's maternal grandfather. The tellings differ on the year, 1962 or 1963, and on the place, Los Alamos, Albuquerque or the Sandia complex.
